text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure (hypertension) is officially diagnosed when your numbers are consistently at or above 130/80 mm Hg according to guidelines from the American Heart Association and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

snippet_links.text: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text_blocks.snippet: Blood pressure readings include two numbers:

list.snippet: Systolic (top number): The pressure in your arteries when your heart beats.
Diastolic (bottom number): The pressure in your arteries when your heart rests between beats.
Elevated: 120–129 mm Hg (systolic) and less than 80 mm Hg (diastolic)
Stage 1 Hypertension: 130–139 mm Hg (systolic) or 80–89 mm Hg (diastolic)
Stage 2 Hypertension: 140 mm Hg or higher (systolic) or 90 mm Hg or higher (diastolic)
Severe Hypertension / Hypertensive Crisis (Emergency): Higher than 180 mm Hg (systolic) and/or higher than 120 mm Hg (diastolic)
Severe Hypertension (No Symptoms): If your reading is above 180/120 mm Hg but you feel fine, rest for a few minutes and retest. If it remains high, contact your healthcare provider right away.

Hypertensive Emergency (With Symptoms): If your reading is above 180/120 mm Hg and you experience warning signs like chest pain, shortness of breath, sudden confusion, visual changes, or numbness/weakness, call 911 immediately.
